properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

necessary.

* WHERE...Northwestern Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing Between 2
and 4 inches of rain have fallen since Thursday morning.

creeks and streams.

Hesperus, Breen, Vallecito, Mayday, Kline, Marvel, Tiffany,

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 11:16AM AKDT until October 26 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 40 mph southwest winds
with gusts up to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...7 PM Sunday to 7 AM AKDT Monday, highest water levels
expected around midnight Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Relatively, the area to see higher water
levels is expected to be Kipnuk. The most likely scenario is for
water levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide
line. Kwigillingok may see water levels of 1.0 to 2.0 ft above
the normal highest tide line. The peak will be around midnight
Monday morning, coinciding with high tide. Following this
system, steady southwesterly flow is expected to continue for
the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through Tuesday, which may slow
the ability for flood waters to recede.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.
